Title: Mata Hari and Treaty of Laibach

Messages.Author: Emiliano Imeroni
Messages.Body:
Hello,

Treaty of Laibach:
"Requires both Follower of Set and Tremere."

Mata Hari:
"You and she may play cards that require a sect
and/or clan as if she were of that required sect and/or clan."

My impression is that Mata Hari can play the role of
a vampire of either of the required clans, so that
in order to play the Treaty you need Mata AND a Tremere,
or Mata AND a Follower of Set. Is that correct?

Emiliano

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <0c1175da-c036-4b35...@e60g2000hsh.googlegroup

s.com>, Maegnar <Mae...@gmail.com> writes:
>> >> Mata Hari:
>> >> "You and she may play cards that require a sect
>> >> and/or clan as if she were of that required sect and/or clan."
>

>But can Mata Hari _alone_ be enough to play Treaty?

No. When you play Treaty of Laibach, it's a card that requires a clan
(in fact, two clans). So you can play it as if Mata was a member of one
of the clans. So you pick Tremere, say. Okay. Treaty of Laibach sees
Mata as a Tremere - "that required... clan" - for the purposes of
playing the card. It doesn't see her as a Setite, because she's a
Tremere.

Note: this happens even if you have Clan Impersonated Mata to the other
clan. When you play the card, it sees Mata as whatever clan you pretend
she is.

Messages.Author: Thrall of Arika
Messages.Body:


The symbols on the side are pretty much just reminder flags. It's the
text on the card that counts. Reindoctrination and Derange require
only one of the two clans represented by the clan symbols, Treaty of
Laibach specially states both clans are needed. Parallels to this
exist with various Anarch and Bloodline Discipline cards versus Dual
Discipline cards. You don't need all three disciplines to play
Diversion, but you do need both disciplines to play Forced March.

Chris, Thrall of Arika
